id_and_class.summary: Michel Henry argues that consciousness at its root is Life feeling itself: an immediate, invisible self-affection with no distance between what feels and what is felt. Awareness of objects in a world, which earlier phenomenologists took as basic, depends on this prior affective self-revelation. Phenomenal consciousness is therefore pathos, the suffering and enjoying in which life is given to itself, and it is the condition for anything, the physical included, to appear.

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is auto-affection: the first-person, pre-objective self-feeling by which a living being feels itself living, given in affects such as suffering, effort, joy, and desire.
conceptual_ground.ontological_status: Phenomenological monism of Life (theistic in later work)
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Henry separates flesh (chair), the invisible, felt material in which life arrives in itself, from the visible body (corps) studied as an object. The objective body is real but founded on the prior reality of the flesh.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable. Self-affection is the a priori condition for anything to appear, so Henry inverts the question of how physical processes generate experience.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Subjectivity manifests itself without leaving itself, with no relation, gap, or otherness inside it. Intentionality is real but secondary: world-directed awareness presupposes this non-intentional self-revelation.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Phenomenal character is pathos, the affective tonality in which life is given to itself before any object. Henry makes the impression, not intentional form, the core of phenomenality, which he calls material phenomenology.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Life as radical immanence; two modes of appearing (the visible world and the invisible self-revelation of Life); the subjective body of effort and the ‘I can’. In his final period, Life is identified with God.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Life is known only from within, by living it. It never appears as an object, so third-person science sees living bodies and behaviors but not Life itself.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A foundational relation: worldly, outward manifestation rests on a prior inner self-appearing in affectivity. Invisibility here means the first form of phenomenality, not its absence and not the unconscious.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal (as affective self-givenness); pre-reflective self-awareness; embodiment; the ground of intentionality.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: The duplicity of appearing: alongside the visible appearing of objects at a distance, there is an invisible self-revelation of Life that grounds it.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: In living subjects, felt as flesh from within. Life itself has no place among objects in the world.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Following Maine de Biran, the subjective body knows itself in effort and the ‘I can’, so bodily power is lived from within before it is observed from outside.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Self-affection has no internal separation, so its unity is given, not assembled.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Henry denies that original phenomenal consciousness is representation, access, or cognition; representation belongs to the secondary, worldly mode of appearing.
core_claims_and_evidence: Western philosophy, phenomenology included, assumed only one mode of appearing (exteriority and distance), which Henry calls ontological monism.
Husserl's intentionality, Heidegger's being-in-the-world, and Sartre's for-itself all place consciousness in a horizon of exteriority and miss its affective self-revelation.
Affectivity is the transcendental condition of intentionality, not its content.
Henry's flesh admits no reversibility between sentient and sensible, unlike Merleau-Ponty's, because reversibility would reintroduce distance.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Phenomenological (radical or material phenomenology), extended into theology in later work.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Dan Zahavi, who credits Henry as a decisive theorist of pre-reflective self-awareness, objects that an immanence excluding all otherness makes intersubjectivity, time, and the world unintelligible. Dominique Janicaud charges Henry with a ‘theological turn’ that pushes phenomenology beyond its proper scope. Others argue his position is a monism as problematic as the dualism it opposes.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Henry never poses the hard problem and would see it as a symptom of ontological monism. Whether that dissolves the problem or refuses it remains open, and his view has almost no direct uptake in consciousness science.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent on its own terms, but the late identification of Life with God puts pressure on the method's neutrality.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since consciousness here is Life's self-feeling in flesh, a machine known only through its visible operations offers no basis for it on Henry's view. Henry did not address machines directly.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: In his final period the self is given to itself in a Life it does not ground, identified with God, which opens a theological horizon, but Henry's account does not spell out personal survival.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: It follows from his late view that each self is generated in divine Life, so meaning is grounded beyond human projects.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Life never appears as an object or pattern, so copying a body's visible organization or information would not carry its self-affection.
